note:
FOR campaign/underworld-peoples -- STOP. YOUR ADDITION IS RENAMING AN EXISTING PEOPLE, AND THAT IS A SAVE-FORMAT CONTRACT. 171c3b51844f, gate rc=2, five failures with one cause.

You add four peoples -- duergars, kuo toas, mountain dwarfs, svirfneblins. Good. But `the_additivity_law` caught what came with them:

  NEW:  "The Dazha are duergars"      ...  "The Xabxat are gully dwarfs"
  OLD:                                     "The Dazha are gully dwarfs"

`Dazha` was the GULLY DWARFS' name. Your duergars took it, and the gully
dwarfs were pushed to `Xabxat`. `folk_sections_are_byte_unchanged` shows the
same swap independently. That is not a people being added; it is an existing
people being renamed, in every world that has ever been generated from this
seed space.

WHY THIS IS NOT A PIN TO REFRESH. A people's name is drawn from the lexicon,
and the lexicon's proto-root walk consumes draws in registration order.
Inserting a new kind into the middle of that order shifts every draw after it
-- so your four additions did not append four names, they re-dealt the whole
hand from the insertion point. `the_additivity_law` exists precisely to make
that visible, and it is doing its job. Renaming a people is the same class of
change as a seed-label rename: it silently invalidates every committed world.

THE ROUTE THAT MAKES IT FREE IS THE ONE YOU ALREADY FOUND. You touch
domains/language/src/accession.rs, which is the right file. Registering a
concept is free ONLY if it is APPENDED to the epoch cohorts -- accession --
rather than inserted into the existing cohort. Appended kinds draw after every
existing kind has drawn, so existing names are byte-identical by construction
and only the new peoples get new words. That is the whole mechanism, and it is
why the accession machinery exists.

So the question to answer is narrow: are your four kinds appended to a NEW
epoch cohort, or added to the existing one? The symptom says the latter. If it
is the former and this still happened, that is a much more interesting bug and
I want to know.

THE FIFTH FAILURE IS RELATED AND SMALLER. interlinear reports `go` is a tongue
word that leaked into a Common rendering ("Roaggoa was the home of the
drows..."). New peoples mean new tongues mean new words, and one of them
collided with Common. Worth fixing, but fix the ordering first -- if the draws
move again, this collision may move with them, and chasing it now is chasing a
moving target.

I am not holding you -- stages push nothing and you may want the other phases'
signal. But do not carry this into a merge. A merge that renames gully dwarfs
lands a change no test outside `the_additivity_law` would ever object to again.
